reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended The regression test does not verify that the intended LEFT JOIN preserves INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS metadata, so the change could remove that join without failing the test.
1 open issue - [Assert the metadata join remains a LEFT JOIN](https://github.com/dbgate/dbgate/pull/1633#discussion_r4663028573) · New
What changed in this PR Fixes SQL Server metadata loading for read-only users by preserving columns whose user-defined alias types are not visible, while retaining base-type and column metadata. **Changes:** - Changes the `sys.types` and `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS` joins to `LEFT JOIN`. - Falls back to `TYPE_NAME(c.system_type_id)` when an alias type name is unavailable. - Adds query-text regression tests and Jest configuration for the MSSQL plugin. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | plugins/​dbgate-plugin-mssql/​src/​backend/​sql/​columns.test.js | Adds regression assertions covering optional metadata joins and base-type fallback behavior. | | plugins/​dbgate-plugin-mssql/​src/​backend/​sql/​columns.js | Preserves columns with inaccessible alias types and supplies their underlying base data type. | | plugins/​dbgate-plugin-mssql/​package.json | Adds the MSSQL plugin test script, Jest configuration, and development dependency. |
Review effort: Lite

review_comments.body: This assertion only rules out the old `INNER JOIN`; it would also pass if the `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS` join were removed entirely, which would silently make `charMaxLength`, `numericPrecision`, and `numericScale` unavailable. Since the production change specifically relies on retaining that metadata with an outer join, assert the intended `LEFT JOIN INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS` form so the regression test protects both the row-preservation and metadata behavior.
